rules.summary: The hospital may not bill a sexual assault survivor for the evidence kit (PERK), including the kit itself, its administration, and processing of the kit or any biological specimens. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: The hospital shall not bill a sexual assault victim for costs associated with a PERK, including the costs of the PERK, its administration, and the processing of the PERK or any biological specimens.

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor has the right to have a PERK (evidence kit) performed at no cost.
rules.quote: a sexual assault victim shall have the right to have: (1) A PERK performed at no cost;

rules.summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. A victim who cares for more than 2 children living with them may get up to $5,000 more per child, starting with the third child.
rules.quote: The Court shall not award compensation in an amount exceeding $25,000 per victimization; except, that: (1) If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or primary caregiver to more than 2 children who reside or resided with the victim, the Court may award additional compensation to the claimant of up to $5,000 for each child who resides with the claimant, beginning with the third child

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is capped at $3,000 for adults and $6,000 for minor children.
rules.quote: Compensation for mental health expenses shall not exceed $ 3,000 for adults and $ 6,000 for minor children.

rules.summary: Lost earnings can be paid for up to 52 weeks after the crime, capped at the lesser of 80% of the victim's net pay or $10,000.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings may be compensated for a total period of up to 52 weeks after the date of the crime, in an amount not to exceed the lesser of 80 % of the victim's net pay or $10,000.

rules.summary: Moving expenses of up to $1,500 may be paid when needed for health or safety, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health provider, or victim advocate.
rules.quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health services provider, or victims advocate, compensation of up to $1,500 may be awarded for reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety.

rules.summary: Temporary emergency housing is capped at $3,000, for a period of up to 120 days, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, or victim advocate.
rules.quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, or victims advocate, the cost of temporary emergency food and housing for a period of up to 120 days may be awarded. The maximum award for temporary emergency housing shall be $3,000.

rules.summary: Transportation is capped at $500 for necessary out-of-state travel and $100 for local transportation, with a $600 total per claim. It covers trips to court, to take part in the investigation or prosecution, to get medical care, and to get other services needed because of the crime.
rules.quote: Up to $500 for necessary out of state travel and up to $100 for all local transportation, not to exceed a total of $600 per claim, may be awarded for reasonable transportation expenses incurred by the victim or secondary victim

rules.summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid to replace doors, windows, locks, or other items needed to secure the victim's home. Guard dogs, other animals, and guns or other weapons are not covered.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $1,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of replacement of doors, windows, locks or other items necessary to secure the victim's home or other place of residence, except that the costs of guard dogs, other animals, guns or other weapons shall not be awarded.

rules.summary: Up to $100 may be paid to replace a living victim's clothing held by police as evidence.
rules.quote: Reasonable compensation up to $100 may be awarded for the replacement value of clothing of a living victim which is held by law enforcement officials for evidentiary purposes.

rules.summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid for reasonable crime scene clean-up costs.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $1000 may be awarded to claimants for reasonable costs associated with cleaning up the crime scene.

rules.summary: Loss of services, meaning replacement services such as child care or housekeeping the victim can no longer provide because of the injury or death, is paid at no more than the D.C. minimum hourly wage, up to $200 per week and $2,500 per victimization.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.

rules.summary: Up to $2,000 may be paid for a rental car while the victim's car is held by police as evidence. The current statute describes this cost as alternate transportation, including a rental car or rideshare.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $2,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of a rental car for the period of time that a victim or secondary victim's automobile is being held by the police as evidence or to collect evidence.

rules.summary: Loss of services (replacement child care, housekeeping, and similar services the victim can no longer provide) is capped at $2,500 per victimization, on top of the $200 weekly limit.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.

rules.summary: Funeral and burial expenses are capped at $10,000. An older court rule gives a lower figure, but the statute controls.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial expenses, including the reasonable cost of embalming, burial containers, cremation, and the chosen method of interment; provided, that a claimant's economic loss under this sub-subparagraph shall not exceed $10,000

rules.summary: Reasonable medical expenses are covered, whether the care was provided in D.C. or elsewhere.
rules.quote: Reasonable medical expenses incurred, whether provided in the District or elsewhere;

rules.summary: Costs from a pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault are covered, including an abortion or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising the child.
rules.quote: Compensation may be awarded for costs incurred for pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault. This includes the cost of an abortion, or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising a child conceived through sexual assault.

rules.summary: Out-patient mental health counseling needed because of the crime is covered when provided by a licensed psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, marriage, family, or child counselor, or a counselor licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling.
rules.quote: Out-patient mental health counseling expenses which became necessary as a direct result of the crime and which are provided by a: (i) Licensed psychiatrist or psychologist; (ii) Licensed social worker; (iii) Licensed marriage, family, or child counselor practicing within the scope of licensure; or (iv) Individual licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling

rules.summary: Lost income incurred as a direct or indirect result of the injury is covered.
rules.quote: Loss of income or support incurred as a direct or indirect result of an injury or death;

rules.summary: Reasonable moving expenses are covered when needed for health or safety.
rules.quote: Reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety;

rules.summary: Dental care is part of covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Ambulance, hospital, surgical, medical, nursing, dental, optometric, ophthalmologic, chiropractic, podiatric, in-patient mental health, and pregnancy-related care;

rules.summary: Pain and suffering, and the value of property damaged or taken during the crime (for example a phone or other belongings), are not economic loss and are not paid.
rules.quote: “Economic loss” does not mean: (i) Pain and suffering; (ii) The value of any property damaged or taken during the crime;

rules.summary: The program cannot pay attorney's fees for help filing an application. A fee may be awarded only for an appeal.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Program cannot pay attorney's fees for assisting a victim with the filing of a compensation application.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Application page, Information on Attorneys

params.extension: one year from learning of the program if the delay in learning of it was reasonable

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime, or within one year after learning of the program if the delay in learning of it was reasonable. Other one-year windows run from certain post-conviction filings.
rules.quote: The claimant filed a claim under this subchapter within one year after: (A) The crime occurred; (B) Learning of the Program, with an adequate showing that the delay in learning of the Program was reasonable;

rules.summary: Generally the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 7 days, or within 7 days of when a report could reasonably be made.
rules.quote: The crime was reported to a law enforcement office within 7 days after its occurrence or, if the crime could not be reasonably reported within that time period, within 7 days from the time a report can reasonably be made.

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor can meet the reporting requirement without a police report by getting a temporary or final civil protection order or a forensic medical exam, or by reporting to law enforcement any time before the statute of limitations runs out.
rules.quote: In the case of a sexual assault victim: (A) Obtaining a: (i) Temporary civil protection order or civil protection order from the Court; or (ii) Forensic medical examination; or (B) Reporting the offense to a law enforcement office before expiration of the applicable statute of limitations for that offense

rules.summary: If the program finds a victim's ability to report was affected by age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or a health or safety concern, the victim can instead submit a court order, law enforcement records, or records from a medical professional.
rules.quote: if the Program determines that the claimant's ability to report the crime may be impacted due to the claimant's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the claimant's well-being

rules.summary: The award equals the claimant's economic loss minus the amount available from collateral sources.
rules.quote: The Court shall award compensation in an amount equal to the claimant’s economic loss, decreased by the amount available to the claimant from collateral sources.

rules.summary: If the victim is a dependent on someone else's insurance policy, that policy does not count as a collateral source unless the victim chooses to use it.
rules.quote: if a victim or secondary victim is a dependent on a primary insurance holder's insurance policy, the primary insurance holder's insurance policy shall not constitute a collateral source for the purposes of subsection (a) of this section, unless the victim or secondary victim chooses to avail themselves of the benefits or compensation from the primary insurance holder's insurance policy.

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part because of the nature of the victim's involvement in the events leading to the crime.
rules.quote: An application for assistance may be denied, in whole or in part, if the Court finds: (1) Denial is appropriate due to the nature of the victim’s or secondary victim’s involvement in the events leading to the relevant crime;

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part if the victim did not reasonably cooperate with law enforcement, unless the cooperation was affected by the factors in 4-506(c) (for example the sexual assault reporting alternatives, or age, condition, trauma, language, or safety concerns).
rules.quote: (A) The victim failed to reasonably cooperate with law enforcement; and (B) The victim's cooperation was not impacted by the factors described in § 4-506(c)

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 may be made before the final decision if an award is likely and the claimant would face undue financial or emotional hardship without immediate help. It is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If it appears likely that a final award will be made and that the claimant will suffer undue financial or emotional hardship if immediate financial assistance is not granted, an emergency award not exceeding $1,000 may be made prior to the final determination.

rules.summary: First degree sexual abuse is a covered crime. The same statutory list also covers second, third, and fourth degree sexual abuse, misdemeanor sexual abuse, and child sexual abuse offenses.
rules.quote: First degree sexual abuse, as described in section 201 of the Anti-Sexual Abuse Act of 1994

params.rule: Anyone injured in D.C.; D.C. residents injured abroad by terrorism or mass violence, or in a state without a VOCA-eligible compensation program

rules.summary: Anyone injured by a crime in D.C. can apply. D.C. residents injured outside D.C. qualify only for terrorism or mass violence abroad, or when the state where it happened has no federally funded compensation program.
rules.quote: “Victim” means a person who suffers personal injury or death in the District, a person who is a resident of the District and suffers personal injury or death as a result of a terrorist act or act of mass violence committed outside of the United States, or a person who is a resident of the District and who suffers personal injury or death outside the District in a state that does not have a crime victims compensation program

coverage.notes: D.C. Code 4-506(d) lets the program waive its time limits for good cause, including compelling health or safety concerns (not encoded as a separate deadline rule). No minimum-loss threshold appears in D.C. Code 4-501 to 4-512 or the CVCP Rules. D.C. Code 4-561.03 bars the hospital from billing the survivor for a PERK, but no official source I saved names who pays the hospital or says whether the survivor's private insurance may be billed, so exam_payment is left out and insurance_billing is unspecified.

researcher_notes: Dollar sub-limits come from the D.C. Superior Court CVCP Rules (DC-S7); the statute (4-501(7)) lists covered costs but sets only the $10,000 funeral cap and the $25,000 total. The Rules PDF is older than the 2023 amendments (D.C. Law 24-341) in places: Rule 25 says funeral up to $6,000, while statute 4-501(7)(A)(ii), the program's Compensable Costs page, and the 2023 application all say $10,000 (statute wins). Rule 7(b) lists only a sexual assault exam as the reporting alternative; statute 4-506(c)(3) is broader (protective order, forensic exam, or a report before the statute of limitations), and the statute is used here. The Application page (DC-S4) says to submit a DC police report or DC civil protection order and that temporary restraining orders are not accepted, while the 2023 application form (DC-S6) lists forensic medical examination as crime documentation; Tend should follow the statute and tell survivors to call the program if documentation is questioned. 4-506(a-2) also says arrest, prosecution, or conviction of the offender is not required, and being a family or household member of the offender does not by itself make a claimant ineligible. Federal OVC directory confirmed the program website and phone 202-879-4216. Reviewer pass: added the statutory $10,000 funeral cap (4-501(7)(A)(ii)) as its own rule, the $2,500 per-victimization limit on loss of services alongside the $200 weekly limit, and the 4-508(b)(2) law-enforcement cooperation ground for denial. Rule 33 covers only a rental car, while the 2023 statute covers alternate transportation including rideshare; the $2,000 figure comes from the Rules, the Compensable Costs page, and the 2023 application. The CVCP Rules PDF carries no adoption date; its dollar sub-limits other than funeral match the current Compensable Costs page and the 2023 application form. No official source found names who pays the hospital for the PERK exam.
